 PUTRAJAYA: After serving the public sector for more than 31 years, Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz (pic) has stepped down as the Public Service director-general, leaving behind several key reforms at the Public Service Department.
 Since starting his career as a civil servant on Jan 25, 1995, he has spearheaded key reforms at the department, including introducing the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA) to restructure pay and career pathways for public officers.
 Wan Ahmad Dahlan said the system’s successful rollout was particularly significant because it balanced the needs of public servants with the government’s financial capacity.
 “I am grateful to have been supported by excellent teams throughout my career,” he said at his farewell ceremony.
 Wan Ahmad Dahlan also thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the confidence placed in him to head the public service, which has a workforce of about 1.5 million.
 Wan Ahmad Dahlan urged civil servants to continue improving the country’s public service to meet the standards of developed nations, while ensuring that every policy is people-focused and its benefits reach communities at the grassroots level.
 He graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Communication Studies (Honours) from Airlangga University, Surabaya, Indonesia, and a Master’s degree in Strategic and Defence Studies from Universiti Malaya.
 Wan Ahmad Dahlan joined the public service as an assistant secretary at the Transport Ministry. Other positions he held was as Comptroller of the Royal Household at Istana Negara and Home Ministry secretary-general.
